_about: What the model finder shows that no launch file holds. Keyed by preset id, Strata size or ninfer profile; model-catalog.ps1 adds context, images, GPUs and thinking from the launch files. speed is net tok/s at 2k context (code, prose) from README.md: the router rows are one short reply each (README § The models), the Strata and ninfer rows the newest bench-depth run of their section. family groups the lanes of one model, which share its benchmark scores.

qwen3.8-27b.description: Default. Best all-rounder, the most-validated config (MTP drafter).

qwen3.8-27b-dflash2.description: Qwen3.8-27B with the DFlash2 drafter: faster than the default, most at long context.

swift-qwen3.8-27b-dflash2.description: Swift 1.5: Qwen3.8-27B retrained to think less, with DFlash2. The daily coding agent.

swift-qwen3.8-27b.description: Swift 1.5 with the built-in MTP drafter; faster only for short prose chats.

qwen3.8-27b-nopreserve.description: Qwen3.8-27B like the default, but earlier turns' thinking is dropped from the prompt (BoxelBuilder).

qwen3.6-35b-a3b.description: Older Qwen MoE, very fast (3B active). Qwen3.8 is better.

qwen3.6-35b-a3b-dflash.description: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, text only, with a DFlash drafter: much faster on code, slower on prose.

qwen3-coder-30b-dflash.description: Qwen3-Coder-30B with a DFlash drafter: much faster on code, much slower on prose.

gemma4-31b.description: Google Gemma 4, dense; its heavy KV cache keeps the context short.

gemma4-31b-mtp.description: Gemma 4 31B with an MTP drafter: faster on code and prose.

gemma4-26b-a4b.description: Google Gemma 4 MoE; the long-context Gemma.

gemma4-26b-a4b-dflash.description: Gemma 4 26B-A4B with a DFlash drafter: much faster on code, slower on prose.

muse-glimmer-30b.description: Strong reasoner with a DFlash drafter; always reasons. GPU 1 only, about 1 GB spare.

ornith-35b.description: Fast MoE with a built-in MTP drafter.

qwen3.8-27b-single.description: The default model's Q4_K_XL on GPU 1 alone, text only; for when GPU 0 is reserved.

gemma4-26b-a4b-single.description: Gemma 4 26B-A4B on GPU 1 alone, text only, at its full context.

swift-iq3_s.description: Strata's default: Swift 1.5 of the 125B Qwen3.8-Flash-Next MoE, IQ3_S. The biggest local model; shorter thinking.

iq3_xxs.description: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 125B on Strata, IQ3_XXS: the fastest Strata size, reads long prompts 1.4-2.5x faster than Swift.

unsloth-ud-q4_k_xl.description: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 125B, Unsloth 4-bit: the most accurate Strata quant, slower, leaves ~4 GB of RAM (use the memory saver).

inkling-2-mini-sq-20.description: Inkling 2 Mini, lossless SQ-20, on Strata across both GPUs.

inkling-2-mini-sq-20-gpu1.description: Inkling 2 Mini SQ-20 on Strata, GPU 1 alone (the cache spills to RAM past ~56k tokens). Not in the tray menu.

inkling2-mini.description: Inkling 2 Mini UD-IQ4_XS on ninfer, GPU 1 alone.

inkling2-mini-2gpu.description: Inkling 2 Mini UD-IQ4_XS on ninfer across both GPUs: the longest context here.

inkling2-mini-q8.description: Inkling 2 Mini UD-Q8_K_XL on ninfer, both GPUs: closer to full precision.

qwen38-27b.description: Qwen3.8-27B on ninfer, GPU 1: the fastest single stream (a ~4-bit conversion; quality not compared).

_families: Published benchmark scores, per family: source is the publisher's page they were read from (checked 2026-11-27), measuredOn the model that page measured (full precision, never the quant this PC runs). A score's setting is the harness or variant the page names. Only the publisher's own numbers for its own model: no score from another publisher's comparison column. A family with no row (qwen3-coder-30b-a3b: its card shows scores only as an image; qwen3.8-fable: third-party runs of other tests) shows dashes.

deepswe-1.1.setting: best of Claude Code and mini-SWE-agent

gpqa-diamond.setting: the page's row says GPQA; its Gemma 4 columns match Google's GPQA Diamond

gemma-4-31b.measuredOn: Gemma 4 31B, instruction-tuned (this PC runs its QAT build)

hle.setting: text questions only, Artificial Analysis run
no tools, judged by Claude Opus 4.6

swift-1.5-27b.measuredOn: Swift 1.5 Qwen3.8-27B, BF16, thinking xhigh, mean of five seeds

terminal-bench-2.1.setting: Harbor, five trials per task, 131K context

swift-1.5-flash-next.measuredOn: Swift 1.5 Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, BF16, thinking xhigh, mean of five seeds

terminal-bench-2.1.setting: default task timeouts, which the page says lower it

_benchmarks: One row per benchmark a family reports. name is the column header, tests what it asks of the model, higher what a larger number means. Left out on purpose: benchmarks that need images (ERQA, OmniDocBench, CharXiv), C-Eval (a Chinese-language exam) and any benchmark fewer than three families report.

gpqa-diamond.name: GPQA Diamond
gpqa-diamond.tests: 198 multiple-choice questions in physics, chemistry and biology, written by PhD-level experts so that skilled people outside the field get them wrong even with the web.
gpqa-diamond.higher: Higher means more of them answered correctly (guessing scores 25): stronger hard-science reasoning, with no coding or tools involved.

livecodebench-v6.name: LiveCodeBench v6
livecodebench-v6.tests: Contest programming problems (LeetCode, AtCoder, Codeforces) published too recently to be in the training data, graded by hidden tests.
livecodebench-v6.higher: Higher means more problems solved on the first try: better at writing one correct program from a description, which says little about working in a large repository.

hle.name: HLE
hle.tests: Humanity's Last Exam: about 2,500 questions at the edge of expert knowledge across many fields, answered here without tools.
hle.higher: Higher means more answered correctly. Every model here stays far below half, and each publisher used a different judge.

terminal-bench-2.1.name: Terminal-Bench 2.1
terminal-bench-2.1.tests: Tasks carried out as an agent in a real Linux terminal (build software, repair a broken setup, process data), checked by tests at the end.
terminal-bench-2.1.higher: Higher means more tasks finished: better at long multi-step work with shell tools, the closest of these to a coding agent's day. The agent program differs per publisher.

swe-bench-pro.name: SWE-bench Pro
swe-bench-pro.tests: Real issues in large, actively developed repositories whose fixes span several files; longer and harder than SWE-bench Verified.
swe-bench-pro.higher: Higher means more issues fixed so that the repository's own tests pass: better at finding and changing the right code in an unfamiliar project.

swe-bench-verified.name: SWE-bench Verified
swe-bench-verified.tests: 500 real GitHub issues from Python projects, each hand-checked to be solvable; the model edits the repository until the project's tests pass.
swe-bench-verified.higher: Higher means more issues fixed. The best models are close together near the top, so it separates weak models from strong ones better than strong ones from each other.

swe-bench-multilingual.name: SWE-bench Multiling.
swe-bench-multilingual.tests: SWE-bench Multilingual: 300 real GitHub issues in nine languages other than Python (C, C++, Go, Java, JavaScript, TypeScript, PHP, Ruby, Rust).
swe-bench-multilingual.higher: Higher means more issues fixed so the project's tests pass: repository work that holds up outside Python.

ifbench.name: IFBench
ifbench.tests: Writing tasks with exact rules on the answer (counts, formatting, words to use once or avoid), each checked by code; the rules were chosen to be ones models were not trained on.
ifbench.higher: Higher means more answers obeying every rule: the model does what the prompt literally says.

mmlu-pro.name: MMLU-Pro
mmlu-pro.tests: About 12,000 multiple-choice questions over 14 subjects with ten options each; a harder, cleaned-up MMLU.
mmlu-pro.higher: Higher means more answered correctly (guessing scores 10): broader knowledge and textbook reasoning.

deepswe-1.1.name: DeepSWE 1.1
deepswe-1.1.tests: 113 long software tasks written for the benchmark (so not in any training data) across 91 open-source repositories in five languages, done alone in a sandbox and graded by hand-written checks of behavior.
deepswe-1.1.higher: Higher means more tasks completed: better at large, many-file changes without help. The set is small and the agent program changes the score a lot.

jobbench.name: JobBench
jobbench.tests: Office work across 35 occupations: each task is a folder of mixed reference files from which the agent must produce a finished deliverable, graded against a checklist of facts.
jobbench.higher: Higher means more of each checklist met: better at finding and reconciling information in documents and writing up the result. Not a coding test.
